questions.stem: What happens to the current at different points in a series circuit?

options.text: It is the same at all points in the circuit
It is different at every point

questions.explanation: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point because there is only one path for the charge to flow through, and charge is conserved.

questions.stem: Three resistors with values 4 ohms, 6 ohms, and 10 ohms are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, total resistance is the sum of all individual resistances: R_total = 4 + 6 + 10 = 20 ohms.

questions.stem: In a series circuit with a 12 V battery and two resistors, the voltage across the first resistor is 8 V. What is the voltage across the second resistor?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, the voltages across all components add up to the supply voltage: 12 V = 8 V + V, so V = 4 V.

questions.stem: In a voltage divider with R1 = 3 ohms and R2 = 6 ohms connected to a 9 V supply, what is the voltage across R2?
questions.explanation: Using the voltage divider formula: V_out = V_in x R2/(R1 + R2) = 9 x 6/(3 + 6) = 9 x 6/9 = 6 V. The larger resistor gets a larger share of the voltage.

questions.stem: What happens if one lamp in a series circuit blows?

options.text: Nothing happens to the other lamps
All the other lamps go out because the circuit is broken

questions.explanation: In a series circuit, there is only one path for current to flow. If one component breaks, the circuit is broken and current stops flowing through all components.

questions.stem: Why is a resistor connected in series with an LED?

options.text: To increase the voltage across the LED
To limit the current flowing through the LED and prevent it from burning out
To allow the LED to emit different colours

questions.explanation: An LED can be damaged by too much current. A series resistor limits the current to a safe level by taking some of the voltage from the supply, protecting the LED.

questions.stem: What happens to the total voltage when identical cells are connected in series?

options.text: The total voltage is the product of the individual cell voltages
The total voltage stays the same as one cell
The total voltage is the sum of the individual cell voltages

questions.explanation: When cells are connected in series, their voltages add up. For example, three 1.5 V cells in series give a total EMF of 4.5 V.
